Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 1) A doctor appearing in court to give medical opinion is usually:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: A doctor is the commonest example of an expert witness. An expert witness can give both facts and opinion based on special knowledge.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 2) An expert witness gives:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Expert witness gives factual findings as well as expert opinion. Medical experts can explain injury, autopsy, examination findings and interpretation.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 3) Special knowledge is required for:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Expert witness has special knowledge, skill or experience in a subject. A doctor gives expert medical evidence in court.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 4) A shopkeeper near the crime scene who narrates what he saw is:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Common witness gives facts only. He does not give technical opinion because he has no special expert knowledge.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 5) A common witness gives:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: A common witness states what he personally saw, heard or experienced. He cannot give expert opinion.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 6) A witness who turns against the party who called him is:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: A hostile witness turns against the party who called him. He may give unfavourable or biased evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 7) An eyewitness turning against the prosecution is called:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Hostile witness is one who turns against the side that produced him. This is different from perjury.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 8) Willfully giving false evidence under oath is:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Perjury means intentionally giving false evidence under oath in court. It is a criminal offence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 9) Perjury is related to:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Perjury requires willful false statement under oath. A hostile witness may be unfavourable, but perjury specifically means false sworn evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 10) Punishment for perjury may include imprisonment up to:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Perjury is punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years and/or fine. It is treated as a criminal offence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 11) Money paid to a witness for attending court is called:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Conduct money is paid to a witness to cover expenses for attending court. It is not a professional consultation fee.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 12) Summons is also called:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons or subpoena is a written court order requiring a person to appear before court on a specified date and time.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 13) Summons is issued by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons is issued by the court. It is a formal written order to attend court.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 14) Summons requires a person to:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons requires a person to appear before court on a fixed date and time. Failure to attend may have legal consequences.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 15) Summons is prepared in:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons is prepared in duplicate. It is a written document bearing proper court authority.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 16) Summons is signed by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons is signed by the presiding officer, usually Judge or Magistrate. It also bears the seal of the court.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 17) Summons bears the seal of:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: A valid summons bears the seal of the court. This confirms its official legal authority.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 18) Summons may be served by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons may be served by police officer, authorized court officer or another public servant. It is not served casually.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 19) An authorized court officer can:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Summons may be served by an authorized court officer. Police officers and other public servants may also serve it.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 20) Failure to attend court after summons in a criminal case may lead to:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: In criminal cases, failure to attend after summons may lead to arrest warrant. Fine or imprisonment may also follow.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 21) Failure to attend court after summons in a civil case may result in:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: In civil cases, court may proceed ex parte in the absence of the person. The person may also be liable for damages or costs.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 22) Oral evidence means evidence given by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Oral evidence is given verbally before the court. It may be given by common or expert witnesses.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 23) Medical certificates are examples of:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Medical certificates such as fitness, illness, birth and death certificates are documentary evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 24) Injury report is an example of:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Injury report is a medicolegal report. It is included under documented evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 25) Postmortem report is a type of:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Postmortem report is a medicolegal report and documentary evidence. It records autopsy findings and opinion.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 26) Locard’s Exchange Principle states that:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Locard’s Exchange Principle means every contact in crime leaves some trace evidence. It is a basic principle of forensic investigation.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 27) The first step of deposition in court is:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Court deposition starts when the witness receives summons to appear on a specified date and time.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 28) After receiving summons, the next court step is usually:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: After summons, the witness appears in court and waits until called. Then oath or affirmation is taken.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 29) Before giving evidence, the witness takes:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Before deposition, the witness takes an oath or affirmation to tell the truth. False evidence after this may amount to perjury.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 30) Examination-in-chief is conducted by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Examination-in-chief is done by the lawyer who called the witness. It obtains the witness’s main evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 31) Leading questions are generally not allowed during:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Leading questions are generally not allowed in examination-in-chief. The witness should give evidence without being guided.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 32) Cross-examination is conducted by:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Cross-examination is done by the opposing lawyer. It tests accuracy, consistency and reliability of evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 33) Leading questions are generally allowed during:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Leading questions are generally allowed during cross-examination. This helps test the witness’s evidence.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 34) Re-examination is done to:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: Re-examination is done by the lawyer who called the witness. It clarifies matters raised during cross-examination.

Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.question: 35) Final stage of court deposition commonly includes:
Court, Witness , Evidence , Summons,.exp: After testimony is recorded, the witness may sign the statement where required. The court then formally releases or discharges the witness.
